title: Introduce slate-constructor and kernel-fingerprinter for cross-model throughput steering
author: Elena Park
description:
Motivation: We need a lightweight, reproducible way to probe multi-model throughput behavior and attribute tail events to kernel-level signatures without running full long-running workloads. This PR introduces two components: (1) a 'slate-constructor' workload generator that builds compact multi-request slates representative of customer traffic slices, and (2) a 'kernel-fingerprinter' exporter that captures per-kernel execution fingerprints (kernel time histogram + op shapes) from short probes and converts them into a compact signature for attribution and routing models.

What this PR changes (summary): compact workload runner (slate-constructor) that supports per-model mixing, ordered/parallel slate layouts, and conditional KV priming; a kernel-fingerprinter service that hooks into the profiler API, produces tiled histograms, and emits a protobuf-compatible JSON exporter; an analysis utility that maps fingerprints to the kernel performance catalog used by the scheduler.

Why this is useful: teams can run short, deterministic slate probes (10-30s) and obtain stable kernel fingerprints to guide throughput-steering decisions (route to alternative model variant or split traffic). This avoids relying purely on long-running synthetic runs or noisy production traces for kernel attribution.

Design notes (single-string): Slate: each slate is a compact batch of 6-48 requests (configurable) assembled from a lightweight corpus sampler. Slates encode sequence length distributions, token mixes, and optional KV cache preconditions. The slate-constructor can emit both synchronous and async probe patterns and supports controlled inter-slate gaps to exercise concurrency windows. Kernel-fingerprinter: uses the existing traced kernel timing hooks, aggregates per-kernel latency buckets (0-1us,1-5us,5-20us,20-100us,100us+), and records op shape signatures (tensor dims, dtype buckets). The exporter compresses the fingerprint into a 128-byte base64 token for storage and transmission. Mapping: a small nearest-neighbor mapper correlates new fingerprints against historical catalog entries to suggest likely kernel hotspots and an estimated throughput delta.

Checklist: - [x] Slate generator implementation (python runner + CLI) - [x] Kernel fingerprinter profiler hooks and exporter - [x] Fingerprint -> catalog mapper service + unit tests - [x] Integration smoke: run slate probe against local mini-cluster and verify exporter output - [x] Bench harness: end-to-end benchmark showing attribution precision and throughput impact estimates - [x] Docs: README + usage examples + examples/recipes/slate-templates.md

Performance summary (selected): - Mixed-model probe (A: long-form encoder-decoder, B: decoder-only) at 8 concurrent slates for 30s: baseline scheduler attribution accuracy 58% -> with fingerprint mapper 78% ( +20% abs ) - Tail throughput under mixed traffic (p95 tokens/sec aggregate) improved 12% when steering rules informed by fingerprints vs heuristic routing - Typical probe duration: 12s (median), data payload per fingerprint: 180 bytes after compression

Files changed (high level): ["benchmark_lab/slate_constructor/runner.py", "benchmark_lab/slate_constructor/cli.py", "benchmark_lab/slate_constructor/templates/default_slate.json", "benchmark_lab/fingerprinter/profiler_hook.py", "benchmark_lab/fingerprinter/exporter.py", "benchmark_lab/fingerprinter/proto/fingerprint.proto", "benchmark_lab/mapper/nn_index.py", "benchmark_lab/mapper/service.py", "benchmark_lab/tests/test_fingerprint_mapping.py", "benchmark_lab/tests/test_slate_generation.py", "docs/benchmark_lab/slates.md", "examples/recipes/slate-templates.md"]

Changed snippets (illustrative): - runner.py: added Slate class with sample method: 'def sample(self, corpus, seq_dist): return [Request(prompt, seq_len) for ...]' - exporter.py: compress_fingerprint(f) -> base64.b64encode(zlib.compress(json.dumps(f).encode()))[:].decode() - mapper/nn_index.py: uses cosine embedding of histogram vector and tiny FAISS-like in-memory index (fallback to brute force for <1024 entries).

Testing and CI: unit tests for mapping and exporter run in ~45s. Bench integration pipeline executed a 30s probe suite on the GPU smoke harness. CI checks: unit-tests: pass, flake8: pass, bench-integration: pass with a single warning re: ephemeral telemetry retention. Full CI summary included below in ci_checks.

Review notes and decisions: 1) Memory/space: fingerprints limited to compressed 512B in practice; we store the compact token only in the catalog to keep catalog size small. 2) Privacy: fingerprints are structural and do not include raw prompt text; templates are configurable to use anonymized corpora. 3) Forward compatibility: proto includes a version field; mapper tolerates missing/extra fields.

Integration instructions: see docs/benchmark_lab/slates.md for running: 'benchctl slate run --template examples/recipes/slate-templates.md --duration 30s --exporter fingerprinter://local' and then inspect catalog via 'benchctl fingerprinter list --recent'.

Release notes: Adds slate-constructor and kernel-fingerprinter for short deterministic probes and a mapper service to correlate fingerprints to kernel catalog entries. Useful for throughput steering and routing decisions.

review_comments: Marco: Nice pattern. Can we reduce the default slate size to 12 for faster CI? (response: adjusted in cli default and documented)
Priya: How do we guarantee fingerprints don't leak PII? (response: fingerprint explicitly excludes prompt tokens and includes only shape+timing histograms; docs updated)
Alan: Mapper fallback when catalog small? (response: added brute-force fallback up to 1024 entries; included unit test)
Marco: Please add a test that verifies exporter output size < 1KB (response: added test_fingerprint_size assertion)
Priya: integration flake caused by ephemeral telemetry; CI job retried and passed
release_notes: Adds a lightweight slate generator and kernel fingerprinter exporter to produce compact per-probe kernel signatures. Includes mapping service to correlate signatures with kernel catalog entries to improve routing and throughput steering decisions. Backwards-compatible proto with versioning. No user-facing breaking changes.
notes_for_followup: Follow-ups planned: (1) catalog clustering job to deduplicate similar fingerprints (ENG-6501), (2) dashboard panel for fingerprint drift over time (ENG-6520), (3) integrate with autoscaler to surface steering suggestions in Redwood Console.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: misclassification of fingerprint may cause suboptimal steering. Mitigation: conservative default policy (suggest-only), ship telemetry to validate with canary before automatic rollout. Added canary flags and opt-in via benchctl config.
manual_test_steps: 1) benchctl slate run --template examples/recipes/slate-templates.md --duration 30s --exporter fingerprinter://local 2) benchctl fingerprinter list --recent 3) benchctl mapper lookup --token <token> --top 5
